lit.summary:
I wrote the R5 literature target file for the one-loop inner product and Q^dagger = S. It holds 27 targets plus one proposition, each with its source and equation number, regulator, scheme status, the project object it constrains, and a Weinberg–Srednicki two-component form. The LaTeX compiles to 13 pages with no errors; one overfull line of 4.8 pt remains, in a row of the source table. The JSON validates: 28 entries, every required field present. I read 30 arXiv papers from the PDF text at the cited equations, kept as local copies in step2/literature/ip_sources/; [HSW] I read only to the abstract and introduction, and Z05 comes through the existing n4_untwisted.json entry. Where entries already existed in n4_untwisted.json, q1_targets.json or sweep.json, I cite them by id instead of duplicating them. The coverage is:
- (i) radial conjugation: Minwalla, Dolan–Osborn, KMMR, Simmons-Duffin, Rychkov's reflection-to-inversion map, and Beisert's oscillators.
- (ii) one-loop two-point functions: Beisert's thesis, DFS, PSZ, Ryzhov (a position-space scheme without dimensional regularisation), BKRS and BERS (point splitting), EJSS, DHHR, BKPSS, AFGJ/BRvR/EHW/HSW for normalisation fixed by symmetry.
- (iii) hermiticity of the dilatation operator and the inner product beyond tree level: BKS, Beisert thesis §2.5.1 and §2.6.5, B03 similarity parameters, Z05, Zwiebel 1111.0083, BMV.
- (iv) 1/16-BPS: GGKM, Chang–Yin, Chang–Lin, BK, BGKWWY, KKLP, KLLS.

I derived nine results, each checked by check_ip_targets.py (items C1–C8, about 1.6 s, 85 MB): the explicit conjugation on psl(4|4) in the Chapter 2 realisation (Targets 6–7), the one-loop hermiticity identity and its covariance under scheme changes (Proposition 1), the uncorrected-translation frame (Target 22), two B03 hermiticity results (Targets 18, 21), the one-loop dilatation operator on BPS words (Target 27), and the order-g leg-count lemma and pairwise DFS ratio (Targets 18, 9).
key_results: Conjugation in the Chapter 2 realisation (Target 7, derived): X^dagger = diag(-1_2,1_2|1_4) conj(X)^T diag(-1_2,1_2|1_4) in the [SW] (17) blocks, with a basis unitary for the compact Spin(4)xSU(4) forms. It maps (3,1)<->(1,3), (2,3)<->(3,2), (2,1)<->(1,2) and fixes Delta. It is the only sign pattern compatible with a *-representation, and it equals Beisert's oscillator conjugation [B04] (D.16)-(D.19) carried over by the supertranspose. Check C5.

Even part (Target 6, derived): v -> -R_*(conj v) with R the inversion. R_* sends the translation along b to the project's special conformal field (x,x)b-2(b,x)x exactly, and R_*(E) = -E, so Delta = 2E is fixed and P_b -> K_{-conj b}. In two-component form (P_{alpha alphadot})^dagger = K^{alphadot alpha}. Check C6.

Odd parameters (Target 7, two-component form): eta^alpha_i = -conj(xi_alpha^i) and etabar^{alphadot i} = conj(xibar_{alphadot i}). The product of the undotted and dotted factors is forced to 1 by Gamma(xi2^dag, xi1^dag)|_V = conj Gamma(xi1,xi2)|_V (prop:c2-special); their ratio is the outer-automorphism freedom. Then (xi, xi^dag) < 0. Check C8.

Proposition 1 (derived, check C3), in code names G0 = tree Gram, G1 = one-loop Gram, M = G0^-1 G1: (X^dag)_1 = (X_1)^adj + [(X^dag)_0, M]. A change of operator basis a -> (1 + hbar Z)a sends X_1 -> X_1 + [Z, X_0] and M -> M - Z - Z^adj, and the identity is preserved. Consequences: S_1 = Q_1^adj + [S_0, M], K_1 = P_1^adj + [K_0, M], and D_1 is self-adjoint for the tree inner product exactly when [D_0, M] = 0. This is the scheme-covariant form of the R5(c) test.

Frame with P_1 = 0, which the project can choose (Target 22, check C4): K_1 = [K_0, M] and 2 D_1 = [[K_0, M], P_0]. In the conformal sl(2) model, M on level one minus M on level zero equals the anomalous part divided by w_O. This is consistent with Z05 (n4_untwisted D4): if P is uncorrected, K must be corrected.

B03 Table 1 (Target 21, check C1): requiring S_2 = (Q_2)^dagger for the tree-level adjoint forces gamma_1, gamma_2 and gamma_3 - gamma_4 real, and all gamma real for the row-swap adjoint (3.9). So the frames with Q_2 = 0 or S_2 = 0 (n4_untwisted D2) are not hermitian for the tree inner product.

B03 (4.13) (Target 18, check C2): with the B03 §2.1 scalar product the norms are 4 and 18. The matrix is self-adjoint only with the corrected entry -9 sqrt2 e^{-i beta2} alpha1^3 g^3, which independently confirms erratum D5. The order-g two-point entry between eps tr psi psi and eps tr phi phi phi vanishes by a leg-count lemma.

One-loop dilatation on BPS words (Target 27, derived): in every frame, Pi deltaD|_{g^2} Pi = 2{Pi Q|_1 Pi, (Pi Q|_1 Pi)^adj}, where Q|_1 is the classical order-g supercharge and adj is the tree adjoint. This tests D_1 on BPS words using only classical data and the tree inner product.

Scheme-independent targets: anomalous dimensions; two-point coefficients of the R-current and stress tensor equal their free values ([AFGJ], [BRvR]), which fixes the 20' normalisation through Q_1 and S_1; orthogonality of eigen-operators of different dimension ([BKRS] (9)-(11), [EJSS] (21)); 1/4-BPS operators as the tree-orthogonal complement of descendants ([DHHR] (3.1)); the order-g^2 correction for Tr X^k is k/2 times that for k = 2 ([DFS] (2.7)). Scheme-dependent: the Konishi normalisation a1 ([BKRS] (17), (24)), a_l ([BERS] (29)), beta_j ([Ryz] (34)), M2 ([B04] (2.2)), Lambda ([BKPSS] (3.6)), contact terms ([PSZ] (2.5)).

Field conjugation and reflection: [SD] (108)-(112) and [Ry] (3.34)-(3.45) give O(x)^dag = |x|^{-2 dim} I(x) O(x/x^2) and show that the Osterwalder-Schrader reflection Theta is carried to the inversion by the special conformal map (3.35) plus a translation. This is the R5(a) route; the scalar and vector forms are given in two-component notation (Target 5).
open_issues: The task's 'Gaiotto-Lee-Wu' paper was not identified after one web search. The nearest relevant paper, GKW 2403.13049, is already in gkw.json and, as summarised there, contains no inner-product statement.
The phase of the field conjugation on the gaugino lambda (Target 5) needs the fermion real slice, which the manuscript does not fix. This is R5(a) work.

The ratio of the undotted and dotted factors in xi^dagger (Target 7) is the outer-automorphism freedom. It must be fixed by the field realisation, which requires that the field conjugation map S^(1)(xi) to S^(1)(xi^dagger).
Proposition 1 is stated for the Hilbert-space adjoint. Its transcription into cochain-evaluation signs for odd operators (def:o-comp, lem:c7-image) is not done; it belongs to R5(c).

Several project-side translations are inferences [I], stated in no source: that the UV-boundary one-loop two-point matrix has its constant and log in a fixed ratio as in [Ryz] (13); that the 20' one-loop norm is fixed by the R-current Noether normalisation through Q_1 and S_1; the pairwise k/2 relation for the project's finite parts; the two-component forms of the SU(4) 10 operators (Target 12) and of the su(2|3) letters (Targets 18, 21).
The relative sign of B03 structure 2 under the adjoint (whether gamma_3 + gamma_4 is real or imaginary) is fixed only by B03's own convention (3.9). The other three signs are forced.
Statements from DR, DRED or SSDR papers are recorded as statements only: Targets 8, 14, 17, 19, 20, and parts of 10 and 12.
One overfull line (4.8 pt) remains in the source-key table of the PDF.

twopt.summary:
I wrote the two-point function design as a standalone LaTeX file in theorem form: 14 pages, two pdflatex passes, no errors or undefined references. It covers the definition, the separation dependence, scheme covariance, the Ward identities and the graph census, with the two-component forms. The scalar bilinears are evaluated exactly in a script; every assertion and every numerical check in it passes. No dimensional regularisation and no IR scale are used anywhere.

(1) Definition: the two-point function is the limit as eps -> 0 of the t1 t2 coefficient of W(P(eps,infty), I - F_0 - I^CT[eps] + t1 O1(eps) + t2 O2(eps)) at zero field, for operators supported on disjoint regions. O(eps) includes every component of the operator counterterm, the length-changing ones too, plus an optional finite part. Constant terms of O(eps) drop out, and so do Q-exact terms, since Q of any functional vanishes at zero field. Existence at one loop is proved: the only divergent subgraphs are one-loop subgraphs that do not contain both operators, and large distance is controlled by a Weyl-weight power-counting lemma. Order-g entries between operators of different lengths are classified by a colour criterion; they vanish among the listed operators but not in general (O_zeta has a nonzero one with the trilinear part of the classical xi-variation of F_n).

(2) Separation dependence: the scaling identity (x.d_x + y.d_y + w1 + w2) G = -(1/2)[tree(D_1 O1, O2) + tree(O1, D_1 O2)] holds, with D_1(O) = 4(Z(O) - unit {N,O}), Z the log eps coefficient of the operator counterterm and N the field-counting functional. It is equivalent to the dilatation Ward identity. For scaling operators the log|x|^2 matrix is -(1/4)(D_1 C + C D_1^T), with C the tree two-point matrix. The implicit reference scale is the unit of length ell in which eps is measured, so the one-loop finite part is the value at |x| = ell.

(3) Scheme covariance: transformation laws are given for each class.
- F0 (arity-zero finite counterterms): the forced 27/16 term drops out when the tree lines are transverse; beta-directions and field redefinitions rescale lines; the coupling direction gives a factor 1 + (m - L)a.
- F3 (operator finite parts): shifts by phi C + C phi^T.
- F1/F2 (arity-one/two counterterms): no effect on the two-point function itself.
- Gauge-fixing homotopy: reduces to the cases above.
The log coefficients, the orthogonality, and the within-multiplet differences under equivariant finite parts are invariant; the finite constants themselves are not.

(4) Ward identities: under no anomaly, existence of local representatives, large-distance convergence and disjoint supports, G(x.O1, O2) + (-1)^{p(x)p(O1)} G(O1, x.O2) = 0, with x.O the classical bracket plus the one-loop component. The two-point function vanishes on BRST-exact operators. For K, the identity follows from the two S identities and the arity-two cochain identity at (eta1, eta2), which is how def:o-K defines K_1, so the borderline |y|^-4 floating K insertions never enter. On scalar operators it holds exactly when the two operators have equal one-loop anomalous dimensions, and it does not constrain the finite part. A central-element and chirality selection rule picks out the nontrivial odd identities: (a) Konishi primary with O_zetabar, which gives a_zeta - a_K = -12 + Q_1 terms; (b) a Konishi-anomaly identity expressing c_K through one-loop two-point functions of O_zeta.

(5) Census: complete for the scalar bilinears, with symmetry factors, colour and flavour factors, integrals and the vanishing graphs. Graph classes, integrals and evaluation strategy are listed for (O_zeta, O_zetabar) and the weight-3 sector; those sectors are not evaluated. The evaluation strategy rests on three lemmas: only log^2 and log coefficients in eps|q|^2 survive at x != 0 (so zeta(3) from the kite is a contact term); numerators reduce exactly because p^2 times the regulated propagator is the heat kernel; and smearing a subgraph costs a one-dimensional Gaussian constant, log(2/3)/(16 pi^2) for the bubble.

Worked example (exact, minimal scheme): for O_a = int omega_a(iota_{a_a}A, iota_{b_a}A),
G = G0 [1 + unit(27/2 + 4 log(3/2))] + (32 hbar dim g T12 / (16 pi^4 |x|^4)) unit (log|x|^2 + gamma_E - 3 log 2),
with G0 = 4 hbar dim g S12 / (16 pi^4 |x|^4). The log eps terms cancel. The log|x|^2 coefficient is 8 unit T12/S12, which equals the D_1 prediction for every flavour pair, not only for the traceless and trace projections.
key_results: Traceless (20') bilinears, minimal UV-boundary scheme: two-point(O1,O2)(x) = 4 hbar dim(g) [(a1,a2)(b1,b2)+(a1,b2)(b1,a2)]/(16 pi^4 |x|^4) x [1 + unit(27/2 + 4 log(3/2))]. There is no log|x|^2 term and gamma_E cancels. Two-component: S12 = (1/16)(a1^ij a2_ij b1^kl b2_kl + a1^ij b2_ij b1^kl a2_kl).

Konishi trace K = int omega(A_Wperp, A_Wperp), two-component (1/4) int omega(A^ij, A_ij): two-point(K,K) = 48 hbar dim(g)/(16 pi^4 |x|^4) x [1 + unit(27/2 + 4 log(3/2) + 24(log(|x|^2/ell^2) + gamma_E - 3 log 2))]. The log coefficient 24 unit reproduces the Konishi value 3 g^2 N/(4 pi^2) with unit = -g^2 N/(32 pi^2). The mixed traceless-trace function vanishes.

Per class, relative to the tree, in units of unit: self-energy 43/2 + 8 gamma_E - 24 log2 + 8 log x^2; exchange -8 - 4 gamma_E + 8 log2 + 4 log3 + 4 log eps - 4 log x^2; quartic 4(2tau-1)(log(x^2/eps) + gamma_E - 3 log2); operator counterterms -8(1-tau) log eps; tau = T12/S12. The log eps coefficients sum to zero.

Renormalised A|_Wperp self-energy, recomputed: unit (a,b)|p|^2 (43/8 - 2(log|p|^2 + gamma_E + log 2)). Gaugino-loop coefficient c = -8 is fixed by the Step-1 1/eps entry and confirmed by the Step-1 log eps entry.

Masters: int D_eps(x-z)^2 D_eps(z)^2 = D0^2/(8pi^2)[log(x^2/eps) + gamma_E - 3 log 2] and int D_eps(x-z)^2 D_eps(z) = D0/(16pi^2)[log(x^2/eps) + 1 + gamma_E - 3 log 2], both matched by direct quadrature at eps = 1e-4 (ratios 0.99991 and 0.99995). Localisation constant log(2/3)/(16 pi^2) is exact.

Scaling theorem: (x.d_x + y.d_y + w1 + w2) G = -(1/2)[tree(D_1 O1, O2) + tree(O1, D_1 O2)], D_1(O) = 4(Z(O) - unit{N,O}). For scaling operators the log|x|^2 matrix is -(1/4)(D_1 C + C D_1^T); the reference scale is the unit of length in which eps is measured.

Ward theorem: G(x.O1, O2) + (-1)^{p(x)p(O1)} G(O1, x.O2) = 0 under hypotheses H1-H4, with x.O = {S^(1)(x), O} + hbar L_1(O)^(1)(x). G vanishes on BRST-exact operators. The K identity follows from the S identities and the arity-two cochain identity (def:o-K), with no floating K insertions. On scalar operators the K identity holds exactly when the two anomalous dimensions are equal.

Scheme laws: F0 by tree insertion (27/16 term inert on transverse lines; coupling direction factor 1 + (m-L)a); F3 by phi C + C phi^T; F1/F2 leave G unchanged; gauge homotopy reduces to these. Invariants: log coefficients, orthogonality, within-multiplet differences under equivariant finite parts.

Order-g length-changing entries: colour criterion proved; they vanish among the listed operators. (B_w, F_n) has no graph at relative order unit (odd half-edge count). O_zeta has a nonzero order-g entry with the trilinear part of {S^(1)(xi), F_n}.
Konishi-anomaly Ward identity: c_K unit tree(Fbar_w, F_n) = -two-point(O_zeta, {S^(1)(xi), F_n} + Q_1(F_n)) at relative order unit. Konishi-chain identity: a_zeta - a_K = -12 + Q_1 coefficients.
open_issues: The two smeared masters (quartic point smeared by K_eps; one operator line replaced by K_eps), each carrying a log(2/3) constant, were derived twice analytically (position-space localisation and a momentum-space region argument) but not checked by direct 8-dimensional quadrature.
The Fourier lemma assumes each regulated graph has a small-y expansion with remainder O(y log^2 y). This is argued, not proved in detail, for the regulated kite and the smeared graphs.
The gaugino-loop sign and normalisation (c = -8) were fixed from the Step-1 per-graph singular parts (two consistent conditions), not from an independent fermion-loop sign derivation.

Hypothesis H2 of the Ward theorem (local representatives converging in the distributional sense near each operator's support) is stated but not proved. The theorem also assumes the equivariant QME in arities 0 and 1 (no anomaly).

The (O_zeta, O_zetabar) and weight-3 sectors are census only. Not computed: the tree sign (parity operator), Z(O_zeta) (needs the one-loop graphs with O_zeta on the cycle), and the enumeration of the admissible O_zeta-trilinear graphs.

Identity (a) needs the Q_1(K) coefficients of cor:c7-Q (engine E5) and the one-loop Q_1(O_zetabar) along the derivative of K. Identity (b) needs one-loop two-point functions of O_zeta with the weight-7/2 operators. The classical signs (minus or plus 2 in {S^(1)(xi), K}, and kappa_B) are left to engine E0.

The constant 27/2 + 4 log(3/2) is scheme data. Fixing the 20' normalisation by symmetry, to compare with the literature statement of no order-g^2 correction, needs the Ward identities with the protected multiplet and the conjugation, which the other agent is deriving.

Directive R7 (finite transfer endpoint T): this design uses T = infinity throughout. It contains only a compatibility remark (contact terms O(T^-2 e^{-d^2/4T}) vanish as T -> infinity) and does not implement the finite-T definition of K_1.

Nothing was found wrong in odd_components_design.tex. Its formula K_1 = (1/4) div v gamma O (thm:o-KD) agrees with the two-point K identity, and its reading of O_zeta as a Konishi descendant agrees with the W x wedge^2 W* -> W* projection.

conj.summary:
I derived the radial conjugation of psl(4|4) in the Chapter-2 realisation, together with its Osterwalder-Schrader (OS) counterpart, the conformal map that relates them, and how both act on all BV fields, ghosts and antifields. The work is in step2/theory/conjugation.tex, written in theorem form with two-component versions throughout; it compiles to a 12-page PDF in step2/theory/_build_conj. The check script conjugation_checks.py runs 198 checks and all pass, with exact sympy and engine checks where possible; runtime is about 2 min and peak memory 0.42 GB. Results are in conjugation_checks.json.

Main correction to the expected picture: in the project's own names the conjugation is P_v^dag = -K_vbar, not P^dag = K. Q^dag = S holds with a minus sign, Q_1^dag = -conj(Q_1). Both signs were derived (positivity and adjointness), not chosen.

The fermion sign of the field reflection depends on which region the states live in. For OS states in the half space (n,x) > 0 the reflection-positive choice is lambda -> +rho(n)conj(lambda), and the OS conjugation then has Q_1 -> +rho(n)conj(Q_1). For radial states inside the unit ball it is lambda -> -|x|^-4 rho(x)conj(lambda(Ix)), which gives the radial conjugation with Q_1^dag = -conj(Q_1).

The map that carries the first picture onto the second is C = exp(-(pi/4)(P_n - K_n)). It sends the half space (n,x) > 0 onto the unit ball, and the flow with the opposite time gives the exterior and the opposite fermion sign.

The BV transformation {S^(1)(X), -} reverses brackets for both parities, which was confirmed exactly with the engine's bracket. So the representation on observables is minus this, and the R5(c) test should be read with that sign.

All arity-zero data are reflection-invariant: the regulator, the action, the Step-1 counterterms and the Step-2 bases. The cubic obstruction from engine B has real coefficients, as reflection invariance requires. The one-loop statement about the radial conjugation is conditional, with its hypotheses listed.
key_results: Spinor conjugation: the map Q -> conj(Q) from Sigma to Sigma^* is unique given three conditions: it is antilinear and equivariant (conj(rho(v)Q) = rho(vbar)conj(Q)), it squares to the identity, and (Q,conj Q) > 0. In the Chapter-2 realisation it is componentwise complex conjugation. It maps S_+(x)W to S_+(x)W^* and S_-(x)W^* to S_-(x)W. In two-component form: eta^alpha_i = conj(xi_alpha^i) and etabar^{alphadot i} = -conj(xibar_{alphadot i}); the minus sign comes from the dictionary pairing (P1).
Radial conjugation, definition: v^dag = -I_*(vbar) on the even part, and (Q_1 + rho(x)Q_2)^dag = -conj(Q_2) - rho(x)conj(Q_1) on the odd part.

Radial conjugation on generators: P_v^dag = -K_vbar, K_v^dag = -P_vbar, Delta^dag = Delta, rotations of V and so(W_perp) go to minus their conjugates, Q_1^dag = -conj(Q_1) lies in Sigma^*, Q_2^dag = -conj(Q_2) lies in Sigma.

Two-component form: (Q^i_alpha)^dag = -S^alpha_i, (Qbar_{alphadot i})^dag = +Sbar^{alphadot i}, (S^alpha_i)^dag = -Q^i_alpha, (Sbar^{alphadot i})^dag = Qbar_{alphadot i}. On the R-symmetry it is the matrix adjoint, which equals minus the element exactly on su(4).

The conjugation is an antilinear anti-automorphism: (X^dag)^dag = X and [X,Y]^dag = [Y^dag, X^dag], proved by hand for all three bracket types and checked exactly on all 3844 ordered basis pairs. The graded version X^ddag = i^{|X|} X^dag satisfies [X,Y]^ddag = (-1)^{|X||Y|}[Y^ddag, X^ddag]. The real form fixed by X -> -X^ddag is psu(2,2|4), with maximal compact even part so(4) + R(i Delta) + so(6).

Uniqueness: the involutive antilinear anti-automorphisms with this even part are exactly exp(tB)((+-1)^{|X|} X^dag), with B the outer derivation (+1 on S_+(x)W and S_-(x)W, -1 on the W^* parts). The Delta-part of [Q, Q^dag] is -(1/2)(Q, conj Q) Delta. Unitarity with rho(Delta) = -2D, D >= 0, selects the + sign; the field realisation selects t = 0.

OS conjugation in the hyperplane orthogonal to n: v -> -(r_n)_* vbar and Q_1 + rho(x)Q_2 -> rho(n)conj(Q_1) - rho(x)rho(n)conj(Q_2). Consequences: P_n^dag = P_n, Delta^dag = -Delta, the two halves of so(V) are exchanged, Q maps to Qbar-type, and [Q_1, Q_1^dag] = (Q_1, conj Q_1) P_n + (transverse translations).

Conformal map C = C_{-pi/4}, the time -pi/4 flow of P_n - K_n (a rotation of S^4 by -pi/2): C(x) = (2x + ((x,x) - 1 - 2(n,x)) n)/|x+n|^2. It maps the hyperplane onto the unit sphere, the half space (n,x) > 0 onto the unit ball, and satisfies C r_n C^-1 = I. Its action on the algebra is Ad(C) = exp(+(pi/4) ad_{P_n-K_n}), and X^dag = Ad(C)((Ad(C)^-1 X)^{dag_n}); with C_{+pi/4} instead one gets (-1)^{|X|} X^dag. Checked exactly (geometry) and numerically (residual 3e-16).
Fields under the OS reflection: A -> R_n conj(A(r_n x)), c -> conj c, lambda -> rho(n) conj lambda, A^* -> -R_n conj A^*, lambda^* -> -rho(n) conj lambda^*, c^* -> -conj c^*.

Fields under the radial reflection: A -> (x,x)^-1 (r_x + 1) conj A(Ix), c -> conj c(Ix), lambda -> -(x,x)^-2 rho(x) conj lambda(Ix), A^* -> -(x,x)^-3 (r_x + 1) conj A^*(Ix), lambda^* -> +(x,x)^-3 rho(x) conj lambda^*(Ix), c^* -> -(x,x)^-4 conj c^*(Ix). Two-component versions are given in the tex. The radial reflection equals (C^-1)^* composed with the OS reflection composed with C^* on every field.

Action and Noether terms, no correction needed: S^Theta = S term by term, S^(1)(X)^Theta = (-1)^{|X|} S^(1)(X^dag), and S^(2)(X,Y)^Theta = S^(2)(Y^dag, X^dag). No compensating gauge transformation or antifield term is needed. The only correction is a total derivative in the scalar kinetic term under inversion, -1/4 sum_w d_mu(|x|^-2 d_mu|x|^-2 (conj iota_w A(Ix), same)), given in closed form.

Phase conditions: s_lambda^2 = 1, s_c s_A* = -1, s_c^2 s_c* = -1, s_c s_lambda s_lambda* = -1. The ghost phase s_c = 1 is a convention (it can be changed by a ghost-number rotation). The sign s_lambda is fixed by reflection positivity: +1 for the OS reflection on (n,x) > 0 and -1 for the radial reflection on the unit ball, checked on 80x80 Hermitian matrices for both sides.

Kernels, brackets and flow under the OS reflection: Theta Q Theta^-1 = (-1)^F Q, Theta Q^GF Theta^-1 = -(-1)^F Q^GF, H is invariant, and the odd pairing goes to minus its conjugate. For functionals: (Delta_t F)^Theta = (-1)^{|F|} Delta_t(F^Theta), {f,g}^Theta = (-1)^{|f|+|g|}{g^Theta, f^Theta} (checked exactly with the engine), and P(eps,infty), P(eps,T), L_t are invariant, so the flow commutes: W(P,J)^Theta = W(P, J^Theta).

Symmetry action on observables: the BV transformation satisfies [{S1(x),-},{S1(y),-}] = -{S1([x,y]),-} up to a BRST-exact term, for both parities (engine Jacobi check), so the representation is rho = -{S^(1)(-),-}. With the physical signs, the free two-point form satisfies <(rho X a)^Theta b> = <a^Theta rho(X^dag) b> for X = P, K, Delta, Q (in Sigma) and S (in Sigma^*), radially and in OS form; with the opposite odd sign it fails.

Counterterms are reflection-invariant to all loop orders, because the singular part is unique and the regulator is invariant. Term by term this was checked for the Step-1 quadratic counterterm (int(A,A), the (dA,dA) terms, (lambda, dslash lambda), (dc,A^*)) and the (Q+{I,-}) image of the field-counting functional, which is invariant even though the functional itself is anti-invariant. It also holds for the finite term int(d^*A,d^*A) and the Step-2 bases H1..H6 and G1..G5; with real coefficients these are invariant. The engine B cubic obstruction has real coefficients, as required. A theta term is invariant only with an imaginary coefficient, and theta = 0 here. Reflection-invariant finite counterterms exist by averaging F and F^Theta.

One-loop radial conjugation: defined as exp(-(pi/4) delta^hbar) applied to the OS conjugate of exp(+(pi/4) delta^hbar) O, with delta^hbar the full BV component along P_n - K_n. Under hypotheses H1-H3 it satisfies (rho_hbar(X) O)^Theta = -rho_hbar(X^dag) O^Theta. Its order-hbar part depends only on the OS reflection and the one-loop component along K_n (the one along P_n vanishes), with an explicit Duhamel formula. Corollary, using thm:o-KD: for scalar primaries the result is (x,x)^{-(w_O + gamma_O)} conj f(Ix), with gamma = 0 for the traceless bilinear and gamma = -24 hbar tr_g(ad_X ad_Y)/(16 pi^2 (X,Y)) for the trace (= 3 g^2 N/(4 pi^2) for su(N)).
open_issues: The one-loop theorem (thm:oneloop) and its scalar-primary corollary (cor:weight) are conditional. They need three things: (1) the equivariant counterterms along the odd generators and along K_v to satisfy the conjugation-compatibility relation F -> hat F; this holds at arity zero and for the classical cochain but is not computed beyond that. (2) The one-loop component along K_v must be defined (directives R6/R7) and the one along translations must vanish. (3) The one-loop components must satisfy the arity-two cochain identity. The corollary additionally relies on thm:o-KD, which the design-audit notice already marks as conditional.

The quantum adjointness G(rho_hbar(X) a, b) = G(a, rho_hbar(X^dag) b) assumes the BV Ward identity for the equivariant observables at scale infinity. It was proved classically and checked only on free letters. The one-loop inner product itself (R5(b), code names G0/G1) was not computed in this task.

Some signs were fixed by evaluation rather than by hand: the S^(1) sign for odd X; the field-level spinor lift sign in (C^-1)^* Theta_n C^* (numeric, double precision at random points and normals); and the Ad(C) factor (a 62x62 matrix exponential, residual 3e-16). The algebra checks are exact; the engine cross-checks are exact only for n = e_0.

In the R5(c) test, the relation G(Xa,b) = G(a,X^dag b) must be read with rho(X) = -{S^(1)(X),-} (equivalently with {S^(1)(X),-} itself, since the factor is real). Physical states must be taken inside the unit ball with the fermion phase -1; with the phase +1 the form is positive only outside the ball.
The Feynman-gauge connection A|_V is not reflection positive (its n-component has negative norm), so positivity statements apply only to gauge-invariant observables.

No errors were found in odd_components_design.tex for the parts used here. Its outer derivation B (audit correction 2) also parametrises the conjugations that share the same even part; positivity does not fix that parameter, and the field realisation sets it to zero.

Rem:c1-real fixes only the real slice of A. The conjugation phases of lambda, the ghost c and the antifields are new data introduced here: the ghost phase s_c = 1 is a ghost-number-rotation convention, and the fermion phase is fixed by positivity.
